points.description: Backpropagation sends the error backwards through the MLP, from the output layer towards the input layer, one layer at a time (recursively).
points.partial_credit: Half a mark for saying the error goes backwards or is passed back through the layers without saying it is layer by layer or from output to input.

points.description: Weights are updated using gradients: each layer's local gradient is found from partial derivatives of the error via the chain rule.
points.partial_credit: Half a mark for saying weights are adjusted or the error is reduced, without mentioning gradients, partial derivatives or the chain rule.

rubric.notes: Full marks (2) go to an answer that says the error travels backwards through the MLP layer by layer, and that the weights are updated using gradients worked out with partial derivatives and the chain rule, in any wording. Half marks go to a right-track answer that gets one of these ideas but is vague, such as "errors go backwards and weights change". No marks for an answer that describes the forward pass, gives an unrelated definition, or is empty. Technical terms are not required for full marks, but the student should not be penalised for leaving out "local gradient" or "recursive".
